text:
Recent work supports combining item text with behavioral signals, but much of it requires pretrained language models. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) adds BERT-derived titles, descriptions and reviews to SASRec; its strongest textual contribution came from reviews, unavailable here. [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) aligns description embeddings with collaborative signals through contrastive learning, highlighting that semantic similarity alone can miss behavioral relationships. Neither provides direct evidence for an entirely scratch-trained text encoder under this benchmark’s constraints.

Candidate-conditioned history matching is a promising architectural direction. [Interaction Fidelity Attention (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09742) models candidate-to-history cross-attention and processes candidates jointly using linear attention to reduce computational cost. An adaptation worth testing: preserve SASRec’s sequential score, then add a candidate-conditioned attention score over historical items using locally trained title/description token embeddings. Preserve numbers, units, model identifiers and format tokens; compare simple token pooling against a small text encoder. These are proposed adaptations, not established improvements for the four target datasets.

Distinguishing broad content similarity from specification compatibility requires explicit evidence. Token overlap can identify shared formats or model numbers, but cannot establish accessory fit or interoperability when metadata omits those facts. Treat missing specifications as unknown, avoid fabricated compatibility labels, and learn any text contribution from training interactions. Validate the added branch and its scoring weight using the common macro validation HR@10; the cited studies do not establish gains under this exact protocol.
